answer: Last-mile proofs: each key answers a random encrypted ping only over a residential ISP path, never a listed cloud ASN. Sticky residential proxies cost about $2 per IP per day, so 500 keys spend 500 x 2 = $1,000/day; pay capped at $0.40/key returns 500 x 0.40 = $200, an $800 loss. An honest agent uses a home line near the nadir of cost: zero extra. Recycled proxy subnets leave a plume the checker bans within a week; fleeing into a dune of new cloud ranges fails as those ASNs are listed. One key per home NAT keeps CGNAT households eligible.
